title: Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions
videoTitle: AP Statistics Topic 1.6 Descriptions for One Quantitative Variable Distributions
intro: Describe shape, center, spread, and unusual features in context, and justify claims with visible evidence.

moments.title: A complete description
moments.text: Include shape, center, spread, and unusual features in context.

moments.title: Symmetry
moments.text: The two halves are approximately mirror images.

moments.title: Right skew
moments.text: The longer tail points toward higher values.

moments.title: Left skew
moments.text: The longer tail points toward lower values.

moments.title: Uniformity
moments.text: Similar frequencies across intervals indicate an approximately uniform distribution.

moments.title: Peaks
moments.text: Distinguish one main peak from two prominent peaks.

moments.title: Gaps and clusters
moments.text: Look for empty regions and concentrations of observations.

moments.title: Center
moments.text: Give a typical value with the variable's units.

moments.title: Spread
moments.text: Describe how far the values extend.

moments.title: Write in context
moments.text: Use full sentences about the measured variable.

cards.name: Shape
cards.text: Name tail direction, symmetry, and prominent peaks when visible.

cards.name: Center
cards.text: Give an approximate typical value with units.

cards.name: Spread
cards.text: State a numerical range or another supported description of variability.

cards.name: Unusual features
cards.text: Mention apparent outliers, gaps, or clusters without inventing exact values.

questions.q: In the video's grocery-spending example, most purchases are under 100 dollars, with values extending from about 0 to 500 dollars. Describe its center, spread, and unusual features without inventing unavailable values.

work.text: Most purchases are low and the tail extends toward larger spending amounts, so the distribution is right-skewed.
Values extend from about 0 to 500 dollars, with most below 100 dollars. These facts do not determine an exact median.
The highest spending amounts may be potential outliers relative to the main cluster; a formal rule would require more information.

questions.answer: Grocery spending is right-skewed, with most purchases below 100 dollars and an overall extent of about 0 to 500 dollars. A precise center cannot be recovered from these facts alone.

traps.title: Tail direction
traps.weak: It is right-skewed because most values are on the right.
traps.better: Right skew means the longer tail extends toward larger values.

traps.title: No context
traps.better: The typical waiting time is about 20 minutes.

traps.title: Spread versus center
traps.better: Specify the measure: for example, values extend from about 10 to 50 minutes.

traps.title: Automatic deletion
traps.weak: An isolated point must be an error.
traps.better: It is a potential outlier; investigate it before deciding whether it is erroneous.

notes.label: Wording check.
notes.text: A standard-deviation coverage percentage requires additional distributional information. Shape descriptions alone do not justify assuming normality.

questions.stem: Most queue times are 2–6 minutes, with a few as long as 30 minutes. Which shape is most plausible?
why: The tail extends toward the larger times.
A left tail would extend toward smaller values.
The stated long high tail is not symmetric.

questions.stem: Which is a description in context?
opts: Commute times are right-skewed, typically around 25 minutes, ranging from 5 to 90 minutes
why: Neither units nor the variable are supplied.
Bar count is not a distribution description.
It identifies shape, center, spread, and context.

questions.stem: Two prominent separated peaks suggest a distribution is:
why: Uniform distributions have no prominent peaks.
Two peaks can have unequal shapes.

questions.stem: What is a gap in a distribution?
opts: An interval between observed values containing no observations
A difference between mean and median
why: A gap is an empty region between observations.
That difference is not a gap.

sections.title: Write a complete response
sections.prompt: A dotplot of 40 repair times has one main cluster from 10 to 25 minutes, a typical time near 18 minutes, no observations from 26 to 44 minutes, and two observations at 45 and 48 minutes.
parts: (b) Explain which features support your description of shape and unusual values.
(c) Explain why the exact mean cannot be recovered from this description.
sample: (a) Repair times have one main cluster around 10–25 minutes and a right tail extending to 48 minutes. A typical time is about 18 minutes, and values range from 10 to 48 minutes. There is a gap from 26 to 44 minutes and two unusually high times at 45 and 48 minutes.
(b) The high values extend the distribution to the right of the main cluster; their separation by a gap makes them potential outliers.
(c) The exact times and multiplicities within the main cluster are not given, so their sum and therefore the exact mean are unknown.
checklist: Describes the main cluster and right tail.
Reports a typical value and overall extent.
Identifies the gap and potential outliers.
Explains why the exact mean is unavailable.
